nodes.title: Codegraph
nodes.body:
Command that feeds the `/graph` page, using only the standard library. Without flags it reads the Go source of the module and writes the code graph; with `-notes` it reads the Markdown vault and writes the note graph.

## Public functions
- `codegraph -root . -o web/graph/graph.json`: code graph, built by [[builder]].
- `codegraph -notes graph -o web/graph/notes.json`: note graph, built by [[NotesGraph]]; exits with an error if a link, a kind or a source path in the vault is wrong.

## Connections
- Writes [[Graph]]: the code-level document (`graph.json`).
- Writes [[NotesGraph]]: the vault document (`notes.json`).
- Runs [[builder]]: one pass to declare nodes, one to link calls.

## Notes
`build-site.ps1` runs both modes while building `site/`. Long signatures are cut at 200 runes, not bytes, so `ε` or `→` is never split.

nodes.title: ConflictCell
nodes.body:
A cell of the [[Table]] claimed by more than one production: the non-terminal, the column and the numbers of every production that claimed it, in order (the first one keeps the cell). The web uses it to highlight the cell and print all the productions in it.

## Connections
- Recorded by [[Table]]: `BuildTable` adds one per conflicting cell, next to the text in `Conflicts`.

nodes.title: Console
nodes.body:
`prepareConsole() (colors bool, restore func())`, with one file per platform (`console_windows.go` and `console_other.go`). It says whether the output can show ANSI colors and returns the function that undoes its console changes.

## Public functions
- `prepareConsole() (colors bool, restore func())`: on Windows switches the console to UTF-8 (code page 65001) and turns on virtual terminal processing through `kernel32`; `restore` puts back the original code pages and console mode. Elsewhere it checks that stdout is a character device and `restore` does nothing. Colors are false when the output is piped.

## Notes
The Windows file uses the standard `syscall` package; `golang.org/x/sys` is not allowed in this project.

nodes.title: Edge
nodes.body:
A directed relation between two [[Node]] ids of the code graph. Kinds: `imports` (package to package), `contains` (package to file, file to type or function), `method` (type to its methods) and `calls` (function to function).

## Connections
- Joins [[Node]]: `from` and `to` are node ids.

nodes.title: Generator
nodes.body:
Random sentence generation for the terminal menu options 5 and 6 and for the web buttons, for any grammar.

## Public functions
- `Generate(g, rng, maxDepth) string`: random leftmost derivation from the start symbol; from `maxDepth` on, only the productions with the shortest derivation height are chosen, so it always ends, even for the left-recursive `E -> E + T | T`. Lexemes: `x y z a b soma total` and numbers 0..99, joined by spaces. Assumes every non-terminal derives some sentence (true for every preset).
- `GenerateInvalid(g, rng) string`: mutates a valid sentence (drop a token, duplicate an operator, add an unbalanced parenthesis or insert an illegal character) and retries until [[Parser]] rejects it. An empty result (dropping the only token of `x`) is skipped, so the sentence is never blank. "Operators" are the one-character terminals of `g`; illegal characters that are terminals of `g` (such as `;` or `#`) are skipped.

## Connections
- Uses [[Grammar]]: the productions to derive from.
- Calls [[Parser]]: to confirm a mutated sentence is really rejected.
- Builds [[Table]]: `GenerateInvalid` needs one to run the parser.

## Notes
`DefaultMaxDepth = 4` keeps sentences short enough to read the trace on a projector; the terminal, the web bridge and `GenerateInvalid` all use it.

nodes.title: Grammar
nodes.body:
A context-free grammar (the assignment grammar or one of the [[Preset]] grammars): start symbol, non-terminals, terminals and the productions in display order. FIRST and FOLLOW live in `ll1/sets.go`; the constants `Epsilon` (`ε`), `EndMarker` (`$`), `TerminalID` and `TerminalNum` are defined here.

## Public functions
- `Default() *Grammar`: the assignment grammar, productions 1..11. It is also the first preset.
- `IsTerminal(s) bool`, `IsNonTerminal(s) bool`: symbol membership.
- `ProductionsOf(nonTerminal) []Production`: alternatives of one non-terminal, in order.
- `String() string`: one line per non-terminal, alternatives joined by ` | `.
- `First()`, `FirstOfSequence(seq)`, `Follow()`: the sets, implemented in [[Sets]].

## Connections
- Holds [[Production]]: the rules it is made of.
- Computes through [[Sets]]: FIRST and FOLLOW.

## Notes
FIRST and FOLLOW are computed by the fixed-point algorithm, never hard-coded; the tests compare them against the textbook table.

nodes.title: Graph
nodes.body:
The code-graph JSON document: module name, nodes and edges, both sorted so the output is stable between runs.

## Connections
- Holds [[Node]]: every declared package, file, type and function.
- Holds [[Edge]]: only edges whose two ends exist.

nodes.title: GraphPage
nodes.body:
The `/graph` page: a force-directed graph in the style of Obsidian's graph view, drawn with the pinned `vis-network` 9.1.9 file kept in `web/graph/vendor/`. The "Notas" mode shows this vault; the "Código" mode shows the Go code graph (packages, files, types, functions and calls).

## Public functions
- Mode switch "Notas | Código": loads `notes.json` or `graph.json` on first use.
- Node click: opens the side panel; a note is rendered as Markdown with a link to its source file on GitHub, a code node shows signature, doc and snippet.
- Search, kind filters, "Ajustar à tela".

## Connections
- Reads [[NotesGraph]]: `notes.json`, written by `codegraph -notes`.
- Reads [[Graph]]: `graph.json`, written by `codegraph`.
- Renders bodies with [[MiniMarkdown]]: headings, lists, code and clickable wikilinks.

## Notes
Node size follows the link count; labels fade in with the zoom (hubs first); hovering a node dims everything but its neighbors. Dark by default, light with `prefers-color-scheme: light`; the CSS colors are read once and cached until the color scheme changes. The URL hash names the open node (`#notas/<nota>` or `#codigo/<id>`); a malformed hash just opens the notes view.

nodes.title: Lexer
nodes.body:
The scanner of the sentence, in `ll1/lexer.go`: turns the typed text into [[Token]] values before the parser sees it. It follows the grammar being parsed.

## Public functions
- `TokenizeFor(g *Grammar, input string) ([]Token, error)`: a word `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` equal to a terminal of `g` (a keyword such as `and`, `var`, `int`) becomes that terminal and any other word becomes `id`; digit runs become `num`; a character that is a one-character terminal of `g` stands for itself; spaces, tabs and line breaks are skipped. The last token is always `$`. Any other character stops the scan with a [[LexicalError]].
- `Tokenize(input string) ([]Token, error)`: `TokenizeFor` with the assignment grammar, so `+ - * / ( )` are the only symbols.

## Connections
- Reads [[Grammar]]: its terminals decide keywords and symbols.
- Produces [[Token]]: one per lexeme, plus the `$` end marker.
- Returns [[LexicalError]]: for the first character that starts no token.

## Notes
The input is read as runes, so the reported column is right for accented text. The words `id` and `num` are never keywords: typed, they are identifiers, as in the assignment lexer. There are no two-character tokens.

nodes.title: LexicalError
nodes.body:
Error returned by `Tokenize` for a character that starts no token. It carries the character and its 1-based column.

## Public functions
- `Error() string`: `erro léxico: caractere '#' inválido na posição 3`.
- `Detail() string`: the same text without the `erro léxico:` prefix, used in the trace action.

nodes.title: MiniMarkdown
nodes.body:
A small Markdown renderer for the notes panel. It builds DOM nodes, so note text can never inject HTML.

## Public functions
- `MiniMarkdown.render(markdown, { wikilink })`: returns a document fragment with headings, paragraphs, bullet and numbered lists, fenced code, quotes, `code`, bold, italic, `http(s)` links and `[[wikilinks]]`. The `wikilink(name, label)` callback returns the link element, or null so the text stays plain.

## Connections
- Used by [[GraphPage]]: the callback turns a wikilink into a jump to that node.

## Notes
Bold and italic call the inline pass again for their inner text, so each call uses its own copy of the inline regular expression; a shared global one lost its position and looped forever. `test/markdown.test.js` (`node --test`) guards this.

nodes.title: Node
nodes.body:
One package, file, type, function or method of the code graph: id, label, kind, package, file and line, first doc paragraph, signature and a source snippet of up to 40 lines.

## Notes
Ids are `pkg:<dir>`, `file:<path>`, `type:<dir>.<Name>` and `func:<dir>.<Recv>.<Name>`; a repeated id gets `:<line>` appended.

nodes.title: Note
nodes.body:
One vault note as the page receives it: `id` (file name without `.md`), `title` (first `# ` line), the front matter fields `class`, `path`, `kind` and `step`, the folder `dir` and the Markdown `body` without front matter and title.

## Public functions
- `parseNote(rel, text) (Note, error)`: reads one note; rejects a kind outside `support`, `cli`, `wasm`, `tool` and `web`.

## Notes
A note may omit the front matter; its title then falls back to the file name.

nodes.title: NoteEdge
nodes.body:
A `[[wikilink]]` from one note to another, as `from` and `to` ids.

## Connections
- Joins [[Note]]: both ends are note ids.

## Notes
Links inside code spans and fenced code are ignored, `[[Name|alias]]` and `[[Name#heading]]` point to `Name`, matching is case-insensitive and duplicates and self-links are dropped.

nodes.title: NotesGraph
nodes.body:
The `notes.json` document and the code that builds it: reads every `.md` under the vault (except its `README.md`), parses front matter, title and body, and turns wikilinks into edges.

## Public functions
- `buildNotes(vaultDir, root) (*NotesGraph, error)`: returns all problems together: duplicate names, a link with no note, a `path` that does not exist under `root`, an unknown kind, an unclosed front matter.

## Connections
- Holds [[Note]]: sorted by id.
- Holds [[NoteEdge]]: sorted, without duplicates.

## Notes
The page draws the notes as an Obsidian-style graph and shows the Markdown body in the side panel.

nodes.title: Parser
nodes.body:
The non-recursive predictive parser: an explicit stack driven by the parsing table.

## Public functions
- `Parse(t *Table, input string) Result`: refuses a table with conflicts (one error step, message `A gramática não é LL(1): a tabela tem conflitos.`); otherwise tokenizes with the lexer of the table's grammar, then loops: top `$` with input `$` accepts; a terminal on top must match the current token; a non-terminal is replaced by the body of `M[top, token]` pushed in reverse. Every action, including the final accept or error, is recorded as a [[Step]].

## Connections
- Uses [[Lexer]]: `TokenizeFor` splits the input with the grammar's terminals.
- Uses [[Table]]: picks the production for each non-terminal; its conflicts make the parser refuse.
- Reads [[LexicalError]]: turns it into a one-step rejected trace.
- Returns [[Result]]: verdict, message, tokens and steps.

## Notes
A lexical error yields a one-step trace (stack `[$ E]`, input = tokens read so far, the bad character and `$`) so the screen always shows a trace ending in an error.

nodes.title: Preset
nodes.body:
A fixed example grammar the user can pick (20 in all): id, pt-BR name and description, [[PresetGroup]], author, source title and URL for the published ones, whether it was adapted to LL(1), the [[Grammar]] itself, sentences of the language (`Examples`) and sentences that must be rejected (`InvalidExamples`).

## Public functions
- `Presets() []Preset`: every preset, the assignment grammar (`DefaultPresetID = "expressoes"`, built by `Default()`) first, then 4 own examples, then 15 from the literature. Each call builds fresh grammars.
- `PresetByID(id) (Preset, bool)`: lookup by id; false for an unknown id.

## Connections
- Holds [[Grammar]]: built from rule text such as `"E -> E + T | T"` by the unexported `grammarFrom`.
- Grouped by [[PresetGroup]]: Trabalho, Exemplos or Da literatura e da web.

## Notes
`grammarFrom` takes the heads as non-terminals (the first is the start symbol) and every other symbol as a terminal, in order of first appearance; `|` only separates alternatives, so it can never be a terminal. An `ε` written next to other symbols is dropped (`ε b` is `b`); it only stays as the whole body. The FIRST and FOLLOW of every preset are checked in `presets_test.go` against the hand-computed tables of `steps/06-presets-research.md`. Only `nao-ll1` has a conflict (`M[E, id]`).

nodes.title: PresetGroup
nodes.body:
Where a [[Preset]] comes from: `GroupAssignment` (the graded grammar), `GroupExamples` (written for this project) or `GroupLiterature` (published grammars). The web groups the dropdown with one `<optgroup>` per group and the CLI prints one heading per group.

## Public functions
- `Label() string`: the pt-BR heading, "Trabalho", "Exemplos" or "Da literatura e da web".

nodes.title: Production
nodes.body:
One numbered grammar rule (`Head -> Body`). Numbers are 1-based and are what the cells of the parsing table hold.

## Public functions
- `String() string`: prints `E' -> + T E'`.
- `IsEmpty() bool`: true for the ε production (`Body` is `[ε]`).

## Notes
The empty production keeps `Body = []string{Epsilon}` so it prints as `T' -> ε`; the parser pushes nothing for it.

nodes.title: Result
nodes.body:
Outcome of [[Parser]]: accepted flag, final Portuguese message (`Sentença ACEITA...` or `Sentença REJEITADA: motivo.`), the tokens and the trace.

## Connections
- Holds [[Token]]: the tokens read (only those before the bad character on a lexical error).
- Holds [[Step]]: the full trace, first stack `[$ E]`, last action `Aceita` or `Erro...`.

nodes.title: Sets
nodes.body:
FIRST and FOLLOW as a fixed-point computation. `symbolSet` (a `map[string]bool`) is the unordered set used while iterating; the public methods hand back slices in display order.

## Public functions
- `(*Grammar).First() map[string][]string`, `FirstOfSequence(seq) []string` and `Follow() map[string][]string`: see [[Grammar]]. FIRST is ordered like `Terminals` with ε last, FOLLOW like `Terminals` with `$` last.

## Connections
- Reads [[Grammar]]: productions and symbol order.
- Feeds [[Table]]: `BuildTable` uses the unexported `firstSets`, `firstOfSequence` and `followSets` to fill the cells.

## Notes
Each rule is repeated until no set grows, so the result never depends on the order of the productions.

nodes.title: Step
nodes.body: One row of the parsing trace: its number, the stack (bottom first, top last), the remaining token kinds (ending with `$`) and the action taken (`E -> T E'`, `Casa 'id' (soma)`, `Casa '+'`, `Aceita`, `Erro: ...`).

nodes.title: Table
nodes.body:
The LL(1) parsing table `M[non-terminal, terminal]` holding production numbers. `Columns` are the terminals plus `$`; `Conflicts` is empty for an LL(1) grammar.

## Public functions
- `BuildTable(g *Grammar) *Table`: puts `A -> α` in `M[A, a]` for each `a` in FIRST(α) and, when ε is in FIRST(α), in `M[A, b]` for each `b` in FOLLOW(A). A cell claimed twice is recorded in `Conflicts` (Portuguese text) and in `ConflictCells`; the first production keeps it.
- `Production(nonTerminal, column) (Production, bool)`: the production in a cell; false for an error cell. Production numbers are 1-based positions in `Grammar.Productions`, so the lookup is by index.

## Connections
- Reads [[Grammar]]: the productions and symbol order.
- Uses [[Sets]]: FIRST and FOLLOW decide which cells are filled.
- Returns [[Production]]: from a cell lookup.
- Records [[ConflictCell]]: one per cell with more than one production.

nodes.title: Token
nodes.body:
One lexical unit: terminal kind (`id`, `num`, `+`, ... or `$`), the lexeme as typed and its 1-based column.

## Notes
Columns count runes, not bytes, so accented input still reports the right position. Tokens are created by [[Lexer]].

nodes.title: Wasm
nodes.body:
Entry point of the browser build (`GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm`). It exposes the `ll1` package as `globalThis.ll1` and keeps the program alive with `select {}`.

## Public functions
- `ll1.presets()`: JSON list of the preset grammars ([[presetJSON]]).
- `ll1.grammar(id?)`, `ll1.sets(id?)`, `ll1.table(id?)`: JSON strings for the grammar, the FIRST and FOLLOW rows and the parsing table.
- `ll1.parse(sentence, id?)`: JSON string with the verdict, tokens and steps.
- `ll1.generate(id?)`, `ll1.generateInvalid(id?)`: the sentence itself, as plain text.

The optional `id` picks a preset; a missing or unknown id means the assignment grammar.

## Connections
- Uses [[Preset]]: every preset is loaded at start as a [[loaded]] value with its table.
- Uses [[Table]]: built once per preset; cells and conflicts are copied to [[tableJSON]].
- Calls [[Parser]]: `parse` runs it and converts the [[Result]].
- Calls [[Generator]]: for the two generate buttons.
- Builds [[grammarJSON]], [[setsRowJSON]], [[tableJSON]] and [[resultJSON]]: the shapes the page receives.

## Notes
The JSON types mirror the Go types so that the page never sees Go structs. Encoding cannot fail for these plain types, so an error panics instead of returning half-built JSON.

nodes.title: WebApp
nodes.body:
The analyzer page (`web/index.html`, `app.js`, `style.css`) served at the site root. It loads `main.wasm`, lets the user pick a grammar in the "Gramática" dropdown (grouped with `<optgroup>`, remembered in the URL query as `?g=<id>`, so the section links in the hash do not drop it; an old `#g=<id>` link is rewritten once), shows the grammar, the FIRST and FOLLOW sets and the parsing table, takes a typed or generated sentence and shows the verdict with the tokens and the stack, step by step or all at once.

## Public functions
- Button handlers in `app.js`: Analisar, Gerar válida, Gerar inválida, Limpar, the example sentences of the selected grammar and the step controls (anterior, próximo, reproduzir).
- The dropdown: changing it re-renders grammar, FIRST/FOLLOW, LL(1) checks, table and examples and clears the analysis.

## Connections
- Calls [[Wasm]]: `globalThis.ll1.presets()`, `grammar(id)`, `sets(id)`, `table(id)`, `parse(input, id)`, `generate(id)` and `generateInvalid(id)` return JSON strings.
- Reads [[presetJSON]]: dropdown entries, "Fonte" line, description and example buttons.
- Reads [[resultJSON]]: tokens, steps and the verdict drawn on screen.
- Reads [[tableJSON]]: the parsing table; the cell a step consulted (from [[cellRefJSON]]) is highlighted.
- Reads [[grammarJSON]]: the productions and symbol lists shown in the grammar panel; the LL(1) condition panel uses the FIRST of each body from [[productionJSON]].
- Reads [[setsRowJSON]]: one row per non-terminal in the FIRST and FOLLOW table.

## Notes
All text from the parser is put on the page with `textContent`, never as HTML. The written explanation (why LL(1), requirements, derivation) belongs to the assignment grammar and is shown only when it is selected; other grammars show their description and source instead. A grammar with conflicts gets the verdict "NÃO ANALISADA" and its conflicting cells highlighted. The page links to [[GraphPage]] (`/graph`).

nodes.title: app
nodes.body:
The terminal program: pt-BR menu (1 Gramática, 2 FIRST e FOLLOW, 3 Tabela, 4 Digitar, 5 Gerar válida, 6 Gerar inválida, 7 Trocar gramática, 0 Sair). The menu header names the current grammar; option 7 lists the presets by group, with author, source and URL, and switches by number (Enter keeps the current one). Options 4 to 6 print the tokens, the step table (Passo, Pilha, Entrada, Ação) and the result, then wait for Enter and show the menu again.

## Public functions
- `run(in, out, colors, rng)`: the menu loop; ends on 0 or at the end of the input. Used by `main` and by the tests.

## Connections
- Reads [[menuOption]]: the table of menu entries it dispatches on.
- Draws with [[palette]]: boxes, aligned tables and optional ANSI colors.
- Calls [[Console]]: `prepareConsole` decides whether colors can be used.
- Uses [[Preset]]: starts with the assignment grammar; option 7 switches.
- Uses [[Grammar]]: grammar, FIRST and FOLLOW sets for options 1 and 2.
- Uses [[Table]]: option 3 prints it.
- Calls [[Parser]]: options 4 to 6 trace the recognition.
- Calls [[Generator]]: options 5 and 6 create the sentence.

## Notes
Frames and tables are drawn by `render.go`. Generated sentences use `ll1.DefaultMaxDepth`, the same depth as the web. Colors are ANSI, used only when `NO_COLOR` is unset and the console accepts them; piped output is plain.

nodes.title: builder
nodes.body:
Builds the code graph with `go/parser` and `go/ast`. Pass one (`declare`) creates the nodes and the structural edges; pass two (`link`) resolves calls between functions declared in the module.

## Public functions
- `buildGraph(root) (*Graph, error)`: the whole pipeline for a module directory.

## Connections
- Reads [[parsedFile]]: every non-test Go file, skipping `web`, `site`, `dist`, `vendor` and hidden folders.
- Creates [[Node]]: one per package, file, type, function and method.
- Creates [[Edge]]: imports, contains, method and calls.
- Returns [[Graph]]: sorted nodes and edges.

## Notes
A call `x.M()` resolves to a method only when `M` is unique in the module; a plain call or a function passed as a value resolves inside its own package.

nodes.title: cellRefJSON
nodes.body:
A pointer to a table cell (`nonTerminal`, `column`). A step carries one when the stack top is a non-terminal with an entry for the current token, so the page can highlight the cell that step read.

## Connections
- Points into [[tableJSON]]: the cell it names.

nodes.title: grammarJSON
nodes.body:
The grammar for the page: start symbol, productions, terminals and non-terminals. The page draws the grouped form (`E' → + T E' | - T E' | ε`) itself from the productions.

## Connections
- Holds [[productionJSON]]: the numbered rules.
- Mirrors [[Grammar]]: start symbol and symbol lists.

nodes.title: loaded
nodes.body:
A [[Preset]] together with its parsing [[Table]], built once when the WebAssembly program starts, so switching grammars on the page never rebuilds a table.

## Connections
- Holds [[Preset]]: the grammar and its texts.
- Holds [[Table]]: used by `parse` and `table`.

nodes.title: menuOption
nodes.body:
One entry of the main menu: the key the user types, the label shown and the `app` method that runs. The action returns false when the input ended, so the loop can stop cleanly.

## Connections
- Dispatches to [[app]]: each entry is a method expression such as `(*app).showGrammar`.

nodes.title: palette
nodes.body:
Terminal drawing helpers of `render.go`. `palette` wraps text in ANSI styles or leaves it plain when disabled.

## Public functions
- `paint(style, text) string`: wraps `text` in the style, or returns it as is when colors are off.
- `box(p, lines...) string`: double-line frame used for the title and section headers.
- `table(p, headers, rows, style) string`: aligned grid; styles are applied after padding so escape codes never break the columns.

## Connections
- Used by [[app]]: every screen goes through it.

## Notes
Widths are counted in runes, so accented text stays aligned.

nodes.title: parsedFile
nodes.body:
A parsed `.go` file with what the second pass needs to resolve calls: its directory, relative path, AST, the import names mapped to module directories and the function declarations.

## Connections
- Collected by [[builder]]: one per non-test file of the module.

nodes.title: presetJSON
nodes.body:
One entry of `ll1.presets()`: id, name, description, group label, `isDefault`, author, source, URL, `adapted`, `isLL1` (the table has no conflicts), the terminals and the valid and invalid example sentences. The page builds the "Gramática" dropdown and the example buttons from it.

## Connections
- Mirrors [[Preset]]: every field except the grammar, which comes from `ll1.grammar(id)`.
- Labels from [[PresetGroup]]: `group` is its pt-BR label.

nodes.title: productionJSON
nodes.body:
A grammar rule for the page: `number`, `head`, `body` and `first`, the FIRST of the body computed by Go, which the LL(1) condition panel uses.

## Connections
- Mirrors [[Production]]: same fields, plus FIRST of the body.
- Uses [[Sets]]: `FirstOfSequence` fills `first`, so the page has no second FIRST implementation.

nodes.title: resultJSON
nodes.body:
What `ll1.parse` returns: `accepted`, the Portuguese `message`, the tokens and the steps.

## Connections
- Mirrors [[Result]]: the verdict and message are copied.
- Holds [[tokenJSON]]: the recognized tokens.
- Holds [[stepJSON]]: the full trace.

nodes.title: setsRowJSON
nodes.body:
One row of the FIRST and FOLLOW table: a non-terminal and its two sets, already ordered.

## Connections
- Reads [[Sets]]: values come from `First()` and `Follow()`.

nodes.title: stepJSON
nodes.body:
One row of the trace for the page: number, stack, remaining input, action and the optional consulted cell.

## Connections
- Mirrors [[Step]]: same four fields.
- Holds [[cellRefJSON]]: the table cell this step consulted, or null.

nodes.title: tableCellJSON
nodes.body:
One cell of the parsing table: the column and the production `number` (0 means an empty, error cell). A conflicting cell also lists every production claiming it in `conflicts`.

## Connections
- Mirrors [[Production]]: the number of the production the cell holds; the page looks up its body in [[grammarJSON]].
- Copies [[ConflictCell]]: the production numbers of a conflicting cell.

nodes.title: tableJSON
nodes.body:
The whole parsing table for the page: `columns`, `rows` and the list of `conflicts` (empty for an LL(1) grammar).

## Connections
- Holds [[tableRowJSON]]: one per non-terminal.
- Mirrors [[Table]]: columns and conflicts are copied from it.

nodes.title: tableRowJSON
nodes.body:
One row of the parsing table: a non-terminal with one cell per column.

## Connections
- Holds [[tableCellJSON]]: in the same order as the table columns.

nodes.title: tokenJSON
nodes.body:
A token for the page: `kind`, `lexeme` and `pos`.

## Connections
- Mirrors [[Token]]: same three fields.
